validity.researcher_notes: P3382 and P3381 share the identical pipeline name 'Shebelinka–Slovyansk Gas Pipeline' and endpoints (Shebelynka, Kharkiv Oblast → Slovyansk, Donetsk Oblast). They are NOT two coexisting parallel lines — they are the SAME 67 km corridor at two points in its life. The wiki's own cited generic source (tsoua.com 'Potochni proekty' page, cite_note :0, backlinks=6 — could not verify live, tsoua.com returns HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and url_verifier) plus independent confirmation via WebSearch, Ukrainian Wikipedia (uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/Шебелинка_—_Слов'янськ_(газопровід)) and nashigroshi.org investigative journalism (2015-12-04) describe ONE reconstruction project: 'Reconstruction of the Shebelinka-Slovyansk gas pipeline (replacement of Du700 with Du500, km 1.1-68.0, length 67 km), Kramatorsk LVUMG, Donetsk Oblast', built in 1969 as a single Du700 line, being replaced in-place by a parallel Du500 pipe in five tendered sections: UT-1 (km1.1-13.6), UT-2 (13.6-26.1), UT-3 (26.1-39.9), UT-4 (39.9-55.1), UT-5 (55.1-68.6/68.0). Official government procurement records (ProZorro tender UA-2020-06-10-007174-b, UT-5 construction; UA-2019-09-30-000369-a, UT-4/UT-5 supervision) and a 2013 Ministry order (search.ligazakon.ua FIN87423) confirm this is one continuous corridor project, not two separate pipelines. GEM's P3381 (Du700, 70.0 km) is the pre-reconstruction/original pipe; P3382 (Du500, 54.00 km) is the Du500 replacement as far as it had been captured. Both are recorded 'operating' — if the replacement is complete along its whole length, the surviving Du700 stretches represented by P3381 may no longer physically exist (dug up and replaced), which would make P3381 a stale duplicate rather than a real coexisting asset; if the replacement is only partial, both may legitimately be 'operating' in different stretches of the same corridor, which GEM does not currently model (no start/end km markers distinguishing which stretch belongs to which row). Either way this is a genealogy/double-count risk for capacity and length roll-ups and needs a human cluster call, not a unilateral fix here.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records LengthKnown=54.00 km with no citation. Independent sourcing (Ukrainian Wikipedia, nashigroshi.org, and ProZorro/Ligazakon procurement records surfaced via WebSearch — the ProZorro tender pages themselves are JS-rendered SPAs that return only ~800 bytes to a plain fetch and could not be independently re-verified live, so they are NOT cited as refs, only used as directional leads) consistently describe the reconstruction as covering the FULL corridor, km 1.1 to km 68.0, length 67 km — not 54 km. The five tendered sub-sections (UT-1 through UT-5) sum to ~66.9 km ≈ 67 km, matching the official project title. However, UT-1+UT-2+UT-3+UT-4 alone (km 1.1 to km 55.1) sums to exactly 54.0 km, and UT-5 (km 55.1–68.6) was tendered for construction on 2020-06-10 — the same year GEM's ConstructionYear field records for this row. This is a strong (though not certain) signal that GEM's 54.00 km captures only the first four of five reconstruction sections, undercounting the full corridor by roughly 13 km (~19%). Diameter (500 mm) is well corroborated for the replacement pipe by both independent sources and is fillable; Length is not — flagging as a material spec concern rather than confirming it.
